value.rationale: A covering-radius and nearest-distance spectrum are canonical decoding-geometric invariants of a newly published record code. They quantify worst-case and average separation of arbitrary received words, information not captured by code size or minimum codeword distance. Exact 176 deep holes, radius eight and the entire ambient distribution give a natural exhaustive classification of this specific object, useful for comparing decoding geometry and code selection without claiming a new optimal radius.
